svg.text: Headset breadboard: Kenwood PTT + Peltor on a spare Heltec V4
Same tag name = connect them together. Pinout and PTT circuit from OpenMANET OpenVLM (docs/reference/openvlm/). Not yet verified on our PTTs.
J2-2 is 5 V. Don't connect it.
Pin 1 = GND on both headers. Find it by continuity
to the USB-C shell, then count from there.
Pin names vary by seller. FLT/DEMP/XSMT/FMT may be solder
jumpers on the back (H1L–H4L): set L, L, H, L. SCK may be a
pad on the front. Only LOUT is used (we send mono, L = R).
Desolder the onboard mic capsule first.
Its − pad is the one with continuity to GND.
Too hot? Gain→GND 50 dB, Gain→VDD 40 dB.
3.3 V goes out on the 3.5 mm TIP.
Meter each PTT before plugging in.
with a meter and a plug inserted.
PTT sense + PTT power (from OpenVLM; R3 changed to 100k)
PTT power (feeds the PTT's own electronics)
DANGER Never put this PTT on GPIO0 (the PRG button). Released, the transistor holds it LOW,
and GPIO0 LOW at power-up boots the ESP32 into download mode instead of the app.
DANGER J2 pin 2 is 5 V, right next to GND. One pin off puts 5 V on a 3.3 V pin.
NOTE R3 is 100k, not OpenVLM's 10k. Their MMBT5088 has very high gain; at only ~3 µA of
base current through R1, a 2N3904 needs the bigger pull-up to switch fully.
NOTE Firmware not written yet: PTT on GPIO6, active HIGH. The PCM5102's PLL can't run at 8 kHz
(datasheet Table 11), so I2S must run at 16 kHz with 32-bit slots and we upsample 2×.
NOTE Left out from OpenVLM: the BAT54S clamp diode on PTT_LINE (ESD protection). Fine on the bench.
NOTE Every GND is the same net: breadboard − rail.
Wire list: tick each one off
GND, SCK, FLT, DEMP, FMT, AGND
node P: R2 100k, and C1 10nF to − rail
node B: Q1 base, and R1 1M to + rail
3.5 mm TIP, and C2 1µF to − rail
